delights: The arithmetic is genuinely tight: my five slots summed to 2,095 kcal against my 2,092 target, with 204 g protein - that is a 3 kcal miss and it tells me the engine is real.

The snack, 'Tuna Cucumber Cracker Plate', is the one thing on here I would eat happily and repeatedly: 174 kcal, 18 g protein, $0.83 a serving, 8 minutes, and actual instructions - 'Drain tuna and flake into a bowl.', 'Mix in Greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, and dill.'

When the swap engine could not hit my numbers it said so out loud instead of quietly handing me something wrong: 'Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance - closest was "Torta de fiambre" (delivered 36g protein vs a 46g target).'

defects.what: Every single one of my five slots is seafood - I would be eating fish or shellfish five times in one day, which no real person does
defects.snippet: White Fish 170g / White Fish 220g / Salmon, cooked 200g / Shrimp 190g / Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids 75g

defects.what: The same protein appeared twice back to back in the original plan - white fish for meal 1 and again for meal 2
defects.snippet: High-Protein White Fish & Bell Peppers with Chickpea Pasta -> High-Protein White Fish & Cucumber with Quinoa

defects.what: I asked for mediterranean and only 1 of 5 dishes is even tagged mediterranean; one is tagged western-comfort and three carry no cuisine at all
The swap menu ignored my mediterranean diet completely - all three alternates offered were Argentinian or Thai, and two of the three were over half fat by calories on a profile I framed as low-fat
defects.snippet: Torta de fiambre (Ham 100g, Cheddar Cheese 19g, 31.7g fat) / Matambre a la Pizza (Beef Flank Steak 140g, Mozzarella 30g, 27.7g fat) / Thai fried rice with prawns & peas

defects.what: Two vegetables in the entire day - bell peppers and cucumber, nothing else. No tomato, no greens, no legumes, no onion or garlic. Calling that a mediterranean day is not credible
defects.snippet: Bell peppers 50g, Cucumber 140g, Cucumber 75g, Bell peppers 125g, Cucumber 55g

defects.what: Three of five dishes have stub instructions that do not tell me how to cook anything - no heat, no time, no seasoning, not even salt
defects.snippet: ["Cook the white fish.", "Serve over chickpea pasta with bell peppers."]

defects.what: A recipe step refers to instructions that do not exist anywhere - there is no 'above' in this recipe
A pan-seared dish ships with no cooking fat in its ingredient list at all - you cannot sear salmon in a dry pan
defects.snippet: Pan-Seared Salmon & Potato: Salmon, cooked 200g / Potato, baked with skin 125g / Cucumber 75g

defects.what: Ingredient roles are visibly wrong where I can read them - oil is labelled a carb, soy sauce a carb, fish sauce a protein
The alternates list contradicts itself - the warning says nothing fit within tolerance while the option listed right beside it is a 100% match
defects.snippet: warning: "none fit within tolerance" (matchPct 88) alongside "Matambre a la Pizza", "matchPct": 100, "warning": null

defects.what: $38.64 of food for one day, about $1,160 a month, and the app knows my job is 'unemployed-home'. One salmon serving is $14 of that. Nothing ever asked me about a budget
defects.snippet: "costPerServing": 14 (Pan-Seared Salmon & Potato); day total $38.64; profile "occupationKey": "unemployed-home", "budgetTier": null

defects.what: Applying an alternate the app itself had just offered me was rejected outright when I sent the dish and its scales; it only worked after I echoed the full ingredient array back
defects.snippet: HTTP 400 {"error":"a slot needs at least one ingredient"}

defects.what: Cold cucumber is used as the vegetable next to seared salmon and a baked potato - those do not go together on a plate
defects.snippet: "Serve with baked potato and cold cucumber."

followUp.action: Asked for alternates on my second white-fish meal because I refuse to eat the same fish twice in a row, then swapped the lowest-fat option (Thai fried rice with prawns & peas) into that slot
followUp.howItWent: Half-satisfying. The alternates came back instantly with match percentages and an honest tolerance warning, but the first apply attempt failed with 400 'a slot needs at least one ingredient' on a dish that plainly had twelve, and only went through when I resent the whole ingredient list. Once it landed the server recomputed everything correctly - day moved to 2,062 kcal against my 2,092 target and cost dropped $3.21 - but none of the three options offered was mediterranean, so I fixed the repetition and still lost the diet I asked for.

verdict: The numbers are excellent and the food is not: a mathematically perfect 2,092-kcal day made of fish five times, two vegetables, and recipes that just say 'Cook the white fish.'
